<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `561147d71af21d39e74451e62956e0c28437c0e1` — the merge of head `265a82f18135486bea5619b27f3958eb222530c4` into base `121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 561147d71af21d39e74451e62956e0c28437c0e1 && git checkout 561147d71af21d39e74451e62956e0c28437c0e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f 265a82f18135486bea5619b27f3958eb222530c4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f && git merge --no-ff 265a82f18135486bea5619b27f3958eb222530c4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 121017b91d12602f8db428d3403cb1a638a7b92f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ecffbe8d012b31fa202e2bc5c25858f0ab9b0875`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts

Read: card #33800 (body and all 7 comments, rulings 6895879286 and 6896340775 included), PR #34156 (body, file list, net diff against `86350e125`), and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `mergeObjectDefinitions`, `foldExtendersOntoDefinition`, `withholdDisabledExtensions`, `packagedRules`, `getPackagedObjectOwner`, `applySystemFields` (registry.ts), `isCodeArtifactBody` (metadata-core), `translateObject`, `packagedObjectField`, `valueOverridesPackagedBase` (i18n-resolver.ts), `restoreTranslatedObjectEchoes` (metadata-protocol).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` is doc comments only: right.** Every added or removed line of the hunk sits inside a block comment (3 hunks: `TranslateDocumentOptions.packagedBase`, `packagedObjectField`, the `translateObject` docblock). No type, export, schema or runtime line moves. `i18n-resolver.test.ts` changes one comment.
- **No accept set widens or narrows: right.** `ObjectExtensionSchema` is untouched; nothing new is authorable and nothing is refused.
- **Public surface: the VALUE of `SchemaRegistry.getPackagedObjectBase(name)` changes, its signature does not: right.** `fields` now also holds each field a code `extend` contributor adds under a name the owner does not declare. The by-reference return narrows to "no code extender ships a rule or adds a field"; the docblock says so.
- **Served answers change on non-default-locale reads only: right.** `translateObject` compares each served field slot with `packagedObjectField(base, name)`; a field the base carries now reads the deployment catalog where its text still equals the extender's. With no locale catalog hit the served text is unchanged.
- **The save door moves with the read: right.** `restoreTranslatedObjectEchoes` hands the same accessor's answer to `restoreTranslatedEchoes` as `packagedBase` and, with no stored row, as the source. One accessor, so the two cannot split.
- **Gates: 56 check-runs success, 11 skipped, 0 failed** on this head, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Test Core` 1-8 and the type-check lanes included.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` match what the diff publishes: a bug fix in the value one public read returns, and jsdoc text that ships in the spec's declaration files. No export, type, schema key or response shape is added or removed, so no `minor` is owed and no `!`.

`Clause-②: no` holds, on the PR body and on the changeset. Nothing previously served is refused, no accept set moves, and the one changed answer (label text of code-extender fields on non-default-locale `/meta` reads) is named in the changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Seat item 2 (the reporter's package shape) was not measured**: the consumer repo is not readable from the dev's session, and the shape is inferred from the card. Accepted as an inference, not as a measurement. The filter itself answers both shapes that can be fixed here: any `extend` contributor whose body passes `isCodeArtifactBody` (a package id, not `sys_metadata`, not `_provenance: 'org'`) is carried, stored or not. An org-provenance row stays diverged by ruling. The seat's question to the reporter (which page and version the 18.3.0 Chinese reading came from) is still open on the card; it does not block this PR.
- **`Fixes #33800` closes a card whose title also names half 2.** Half 2 is ruled out of this PR (maintainer ruling 6896340775) and has its own open card, #33952. Closing is consistent with the ruling.
- **Seat item 4 (extender-added `listViews`): answered.** `ObjectExtensionSchema` is strict and its key list has no `listViews`; `mergeObjectDefinitions` copies no key outside its closed set. No card owed.
- **Deviation: suites ran on `c856cd3b7`, not the final head.** Covered: `Test Core` 1-8 are green on this head.
- **Deviation: a third comment (`translateObject` docblock) rewritten beyond the two the amendment names.** Same file, same reason, comment only. Accepted.
- `open_questions` is empty. No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` (hits).** Each changed sentence was read against the code it describes.

- `packagedBase`: "its `fields` also carry each field a code extender ADDS under a name the owner does not declare, as that extender ships it". Holds against `packagedAddedFields` and the spread in `getPackagedObjectBase`. "Its scalars, every field the owner declares ... stay the owner's": holds, the `hasOwnProperty` guard on the owner's `fields` and the untouched spread of `owner.definition`. Every supplier of an object's `packagedBase` (the REST read through metadata-protocol's `getPackagedObjectBase`, the echo restore) goes through the one registry accessor, so the sentence is true for every caller.
- `packagedObjectField`: the three answers are unchanged in code, and the reworded `{}` case holds. The owner's body carries the platform's injected columns (`applySystemFields` runs at registration), so those are not a third undeclared case.
- `translateObject` docblock: holds.

**`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (implementing).** Tried to break the docs' claims against the fold.

- Filter equals `packagedRules`' (`ownership === 'extend'` and `isCodeArtifactBody`): holds, same expression.
- Fold order: `objectContributors` lists are kept sorted by ascending `priority`, and the fold spreads `{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }`, so "a later extender's declaration replaces an earlier one's" holds whenever every extender is enabled.
- `fieldPatches` not read; an extender's `queue` or audit-column redeclaration is skipped as owner-declared (the owner's body is planned at registration); a tenant overlay and an org-provenance extension contribute nothing; the tenant's rename of an extender field still reads as diverged because the base holds the extender's text. All hold.
- No caller depends on reference equality or reads base `fields` for a lock or write decision: the callers are the REST read, the echo restore and the validation-message lookup.

Findings:

1. **should-fix: the base does not follow the fold when a code extender's package is DISABLED.** The served fold withholds a disabled package's `extend` contribution (`withholdDisabledExtensions`, used by `resolveObject`); `packagedAddedFields` reads every code `extend` contributor, disabled or not. With two code extenders adding one field name and the higher-`priority` one disabled, the fold serves the enabled extender's declaration and the base carries the disabled one's. Where their labels or option labels differ, the served field reads as diverged and is served untranslated, which is the card's own defect for that pair. So "in fold order ... as `mergeObjectDefinitions` does" (the `packagedAddedFields` doc), "Same-name extenders resolve to the fold's winner" (PR body) and "as in the fold" (changeset) do not hold there. It fails toward source text, never toward wrong text, and needs a name collision the fold already reports (#28835), so it is not a must-fix. Fix either way: skip contributors whose package is disabled, with a pin, or state the boundary in the docblock and file a card. `packagedRules` has the same gap for rule names (outside the diff, read only): a follow-up card, not this PR.
2. **nit: one sentence of the `packagedBase` doc is hard to parse.** "the owner's fields as an extension's `fieldPatches` leave them stay the owner's" can be read as "the base carries the patched fields", the opposite of the code. Suggested: "an extension's `fieldPatches` are not applied to it". Left as a follow-up; a fix here moves the head.
3. **nit: "a stored extension's" in the `packagedObjectField` and `translateObject` docs is broader than the filter.** A stored extension body with package provenance passes `isCodeArtifactBody` and IS carried; only an org-provenance one is not. The registry docblock says "stored (non-code)", which is exact. Follow-up wording only.

## Review — PASS (should-fix owed before landing)

Head-sha: `ecffbe8d012b31fa202e2bc5c25858f0ab9b0875`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T23:19Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `86350e12` (7 files, +434/−15, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM; the contract face by an isolated sub-agent at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

**Contract face:** `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` changes in doc comments only. The record confirms that every changed line sits inside a block comment. The review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Its record is comment 6903060139 (PASS, `Local-runs: none`), and it carries one should-fix. This verdict covers the rest of the diff at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

**Should-fix (from the record, and I found it independently in the code; delta review after the fix)**

1. **`packagedAddedFields` reads disabled packages' extensions, while the served fold withholds them.** `getObjectContributors` keeps a disabled package's `extend` contribution, which is why #34024's refusal can name it. Suppose two code extenders add the same field name and the later one is disabled. The base then carries the disabled extender's declaration, and the served field is the enabled one's. So the field reads as diverged and stays untranslated. The "as in the fold" sentences in the docblock and the changeset do not hold in that case.

   This fails toward source text, never toward wrong text. Either fix it in this PR:
   - skip disabled contributors, as the fold does, and add a pin; or
   - state the boundary in the docblock and the changeset, and file a card that also covers `packagedRules`, which has the same gap for rule names outside this diff.

**What holds (rest of the diff)**

- **The packaged base widens only by field names the owner does not declare.** The owner's scalars, every owner-declared field (including one an extender redeclares) and every `fieldPatches` entry stay the owner's. #8037's divergence rule therefore keeps holding for everything it covered. A tenant overlay or an `_provenance: 'org'` extension adds nothing.
- **Readers.** `getPackagedObjectBase` is read only by the translation path (`PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS` in `meta-item-read-gate.ts`), the save door's translated-echo restore and the validation-message reader. The validation-message reader reads `validations` alone, so the wider `fields` reaches only translation and the echo restore. The changeset names the echo-restore consequence: a Studio save of a translated read stores the source text.
- **By-reference identity is kept** when nothing is added, and that is pinned.
- **Tests.** Real-registry pins cover the added field, the owner redeclare, the tenant overlay, the stored extension, `fieldPatches` and the later-extender order. There are REST pins for the item read and the list read in zh-CN and en, and an echo-restore pin with and without a stored row. Each of the three ablations goes red on the pins it targets.
- **Changeset.** `objectql` and `spec` patch. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` hold: translation output changes, but no authorable key or accept set moves.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

The record's two comment nits:
- "the owner's fields as an extension's `fieldPatches` leave them stay the owner's" can be read backwards.
- "a stored extension's" is broader than the filter. A stored extension with package provenance passes `isCodeArtifactBody` and is carried.

Fold both into the should-fix round if you touch those comments.

**Gates:** at review time 56 success, 11 skipped, none red, so every check is green.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `265a82f18135486bea5619b27f3958eb222530c4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-field-patch-i18n.test.ts

Read at 2026-11-16T01:08Z. Delta review of this head against PASS 6903060139 at ecffbe8d (by the lane's own reviewer); claim: comment 6904455068; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5; reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

Read: card #33800 (body, all comments, seat ruling 6895879286 and maintainer ruling 6896340775), the PR body and comments, record 6903060139, the changeset, the net diff at this head, the two dev commits `e2c5196a` and `8c317692`, what the main merge brought under `packages/objectql`, `packages/spec`, `packages/rest` and `packages/services/service-i18n`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `resolveObject`, `servedFoldWithLayer`, `resolveObjectLeavingExtensionsOut`, `foldObjectExtendersOnto`, `resolveStorageObject`, `withholdDisabledExtensions`, `withoutWithheldMembers`, `packagedRules`, `isPackageDisabled` (registry.ts), `restoreTranslatedObjectEchoes` (metadata-protocol), `PACKAGED_BASE_ACCESSORS` and the resolve-options builder (rest).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The net change at this head is the prior net change plus the two dev commits, and nothing else: right.** Prior base `86350e12`, this base `2539ad98` (the merge's main parent, also the merge base). Per path, the patch of base to head equals the patch of the prior base to the dev tip `8c317692` on all seven paths. Six of the seven are byte-identical at head and at the dev tip. The seventh, `i18n-resolver.ts`, differs only by what main brought. The merge commit reproduces exactly from its two parents with no conflict, so it carries no hand edit.
- **The two dev commits touch five paths: right.** `registry.ts` (the disabled filter in `getPackagedObjectBase`, `packagedAddedFields` moved above the docblock it had been splitting from `mergeObjectDefinitions`, docblock wording), one new REST pin, the changeset text, and comment wording in `i18n-resolver.ts` and its test. No type, export, schema or accept set moves. The `@objectstack/spec` change stays doc comments only at this head.
- **The main merge conflicts with nothing here and leaves no baseline stale: right.** Of the PR's paths, main touched `i18n-resolver.ts` alone (#34025), in the module header, `ResolveOptions.defaultLocale` and the lookup-order docblock: comment text, in hunks the PR does not touch. #34025's runtime change in `packages/rest` picks the authored language for the resolve options and does not read the packaged base. The `performedBy` change (#34018) and the AI-door confirmation change (#34001) touch no path or symbol of this diff. The PR adds or edits no generated artifact. The head also merges clean with current main `121017b9`.
- **`getPackagedObjectBase` now leaves out a disabled package's added fields by the fold's own predicate: right.** The filter is `ownership === 'extend'` and `isPackageDisabled(packageId)`, the expression `withholdDisabledExtensions` uses. The accessor is uncached, so an enable or disable needs no invalidation. The return shape and the by-reference rule are unchanged.
- **CI: 67 check-runs on this head, 56 success, 11 skipped, none failing, none running.**

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` still match what the diff publishes: the value one public read returns, and jsdoc text. No `minor` and no `!` is owed. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold on the PR body and the changeset: nothing served before is refused, no accept set moves, and the changed answer (label text of code-extender fields on translated `/meta` reads) is named in the changeset, with the disabled-extender boundary added by `8c317692`.

CI is complete and green on this head, so this PASS waits on no check.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Prior ③ flags** (reporter's package shape inferred, not measured; `Fixes #33800` with half 2 on its own card; extender-added `listViews`; suites run on an earlier head; the third rewritten comment): unchanged by the delta, and I agree with each answer. `Test Core` is green on this head.
- **The rule half of the base still reads a disabled package's extension.** `packagedRules` is not filtered, and the new docblock says so. It is outside what this PR changes, and the prior record sent it to a follow-up card. No card number for it appears in the PR body, the commits or the card thread: see S1.
- **Folds that are not the ordinary served one** (the per-package export layer, the enable door's as-enabled pre-check, the storage fold) can carry an added field from a different extender than the base does. The base is keyed by name alone. Where they differ the slot reads as diverged and keeps its source text. This is as at the prior head and not a finding.
- **SQL push-down check:** the diff adds no query, id materialisation or in-app join.
- `open_questions` is empty. No escalation.

### ④ Design judgment

**Prior findings, by id (record 6903060139).**

- **Finding 1 (should-fix, the base did not follow the fold for a disabled code extender): resolved for fields.** With the higher-priority adder disabled, the base now carries the enabled extender's declaration, the one the fold serves. I checked each served reader of the fold. `resolveObject`, `servedFoldWithLayer`, `resolveObjectLeavingExtensionsOut` and `foldObjectExtendersOnto` all withhold through `withholdDisabledExtensions`, and each takes a withheld-only field off a base body that already carries it. So no served read carries a disabled extender's added field while the base lacks it, and none carries the base's field from a different enabled extender in the ordinary fold. The storage fold keeps the columns by design and is not a translated read. The save door reads the same accessor, so read and write cannot split. The base only decides whether a slot is translated; it never removes a field from a served body, so no reader drops a field it should serve. The pin is the new REST case: it asserts its premise (the fold serves the enabled extender's label), the base's label, and the translated label and option labels. Its control is the enabled twin of the same fixture in `protocol-packaged-object-base.test.ts` (a later enabled extender wins in the base and in the fold). Without the filter the base would hold the disabled extender's label, so the pin's base assertion and its translation assertions cannot hold. That is read from the code; nothing was run.
- **Finding 2 (nit, the `packagedBase` sentence that read backwards): resolved.** It now reads "an extension's `fieldPatches` are never folded in, so a patched owner field still reads as diverged", which matches the code.
